evidence.claim: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.title: Pakistan picks central bank veteran Jameel Ahmad as new governor
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific high-level appointment with institutional facts about the appointee.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to the Sharif government's macro-management decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The governor was appointed by the Sharif government, but the SBP remained an institutionally separate actor.
contrary_evidence: Appointment quality does not by itself prove the quality of later monetary policy.

evidence.claim: On the prime minister's advice, Ahad Cheema was appointed adviser to the PM on establishment; the report also notes his prior NAB arrest and inquiries linked to Ashiana-i-Iqbal and related cases.
evidence.title: President Alvi appoints Ahad Cheema as adviser to the PM on establishment
evidence.excerpt: On the prime minister's advice, Ahad Cheema was appointed adviser to the PM on establishment; the report also notes his prior NAB arrest and inquiries linked to Ashiana-i-Iqbal and related cases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of a formal PM-linked appointment and the appointee's corruption-case background.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's appointment power; the appointment cuts both ways because Cheema is a professional bureaucrat but also a controversial insider with pending case history.
contrary_evidence: A career bureaucrat appointment can be read as competence-oriented, but the corruption baggage weakens the purity of that signal.

evidence.claim: A special court acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hamza Shehbaz in the Rs16 billion money laundering case after the FIA told the court that no direct transaction had been made from benami accounts into their bank accounts.
evidence.title: Lahore court acquits PM Shehbaz, son Hamza in Rs16bn money laundering case
evidence.excerpt: A special court acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hamza Shehbaz in the Rs16 billion money laundering case after the FIA told the court that no direct transaction had been made from benami accounts into their bank accounts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous court report on a dispositive judicial outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sharif because it resolves a major corruption accusation against him and his son, although it does not affirmively prove virtue beyond the case outcome.
contrary_evidence: An acquittal removes proof of this case, but it does not automatically establish broad personal integrity in all domains.

evidence.claim: The trial judge said the record was silent on any benefit to Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza from the alleged benami accounts, found no nexus between them and the accounts, and said there was no probability of conviction.
evidence.title: FIA failed to link Shehbaz, Hamza to benami accounts: judge
evidence.excerpt: The trial judge said the record was silent on any benefit to Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza from the alleged benami accounts, found no nexus between them and the accounts, and said there was no probability of conviction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a detailed written judicial verdict.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the ruler because the verdict addresses allegations against him and his son, but it remains case-specific rather than a full integrity audit.
contrary_evidence: The verdict concerns one case and does not settle all corruption allegations about the family.

evidence.claim: The Daily Mail apologized to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, stating that he had never been accused by NAB of wrongdoing in relation to British public money or DFID grant aid and retracting the accusation that he stole aid money for earthquake victims.
evidence.title: Not accused of any wrongdoing: Daily Mail apologises to PM Shehbaz for false corruption allegation
evidence.excerpt: The Daily Mail apologized to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, stating that he had never been accused by NAB of wrongdoing in relation to British public money or DFID grant aid and retracting the accusation that he stole aid money for earthquake victims.
evidence.source_locator: lead and apology quotation in the article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The piece reports an explicit correction and apology from the publication, though the article is a secondary report rather than the publisher's original notice.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective correction during 2022; relevant because it concerns a major corruption accusation against Sharif.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not a ruler action, but it is an independent correction that materially weakens one prominent public corruption allegation against him.
contrary_evidence: The apology concerns one historical allegation and does not resolve the separate domestic money-laundering cases.

evidence.claim: The ECP data released in 2022 showed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's assets at about Rs246 million, including London property, a small bank balance, liabilities, and a loan from his son Suleman.
evidence.title: ECP releases data of assets owned by PM Shehbaz, Imran Khan, Zardari, and others
evidence.excerpt: The ECP data released in 2022 showed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's assets at about Rs246 million, including London property, a small bank balance, liabilities, and a loan from his son Suleman.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report is based on an official ECP asset disclosure, but the page is a media summary rather than the underlying filing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's own disclosure and relevant to transparency, though it does not by itself prove clean governance or the absence of conflicts.
contrary_evidence: Public asset disclosure is positive for transparency but not proof that no hidden conflicts or family entanglements existed.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
